If you can find blue potatoes#give those a try too. Instead of lime or lemon juice#some cooks use bitter orange juice.#
"•Fillings: Chicken or seafood salads bound together with mayonnaise are very common causa fillings. You can also use shredded or whole lettuce leaves or any of the filling ingredients to garnish.#
"•Sauces: Sauces are often drizzled over a finished causa. "•A popular alternative way to form the causa is rolled up like a jellyroll#or pionono. Spread the potatoes into a smooth rectangle over a layer of plastic wrap. Spread the filling over the potatoes. Lift the plastic wrap from one end of the potatoes and roll the potatoes up over the filling. Place seam-side down on a serving platter#garnish and serve in slices. Causa rellena can also be formed in a springform pan or as individual portions.#•Causa Limeña: A causa from Lima served with a fish filling or with fried fish on the side."
